title: Reason Code 73/267/283/293/296: the client certificate lacks the Client Authentication purpose
plain_english: EAP-TLS: the device presented a certificate that is valid and trusted, but its Enhanced Key Usage does not include Client Authentication (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2), so NPS refuses to accept it as proof of identity. Usually a template problem, or the supplicant picking the wrong certificate from a store that holds several.

any: not configured with the Client Authentication purpose
does not contain the Client Authentication purpose

causes.cause: The certificate template does not include Client Authentication in Application Policies.
causes.next_check: On the CA, open the template's Extensions tab > Application Policies; add Client Authentication, then re-enroll the affected devices (existing certificates do not change).

causes.cause: The device holds several certificates and the supplicant chose one meant for something else (a code-signing, S/MIME, or web-server certificate).
causes.next_check: In the Wi-Fi profile's EAP-TLS settings, restrict certificate selection by issuer or EKU (Windows: 'Use simple certificate selection' off, then filter); on the device check which certificate the profile actually uses.
